structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, no amphibian species (frogs, toads, newts, salamanders) is recorded as native to any island that has never been connected to a continent, while introduced amphibians are recorded as established on several of those same islands.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Across a list of oceanic islands or archipelagos fixed before looking at the data, at most 1 in 20 (5% or fewer) has one or more native amphibian species in AmphibiaWeb's species-by-country/region records. Native means a species whose range includes the island and that is not flagged as introduced. In addition, at least 3 of the listed islands have an established introduced amphibian species (recorded as introduced in AmphibiaWeb species accounts). The pre-registered list is: Hawaii, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, Galapagos, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Mauritius, Reunion, Rodrigues, Society Islands, Marquesas, Tuamotus, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Bermuda, Iceland. Any island on the list that turns out to be continental in origin is replaced in the list before analysis, with the replacement documented.
structured_output.fail_criterion: More than 2 of the 20 listed islands (over 10%) have one or more native amphibian species. That would show 'strictly true' is false as a generalization. Alternatively, fewer than 3 islands have documented established introduced amphibians. In that case the 'introduced frogs thrive' premise is not supported. Between these results (exactly 2 islands with natives) the claim is judged not strictly true but largely true.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Batrachians' is read as Darwin used it, meaning frogs, toads and newts. Modern Amphibia also includes salamanders and caecilians, so the test counts all Amphibia and reports Anura and Caudata separately. 'Oceanic islands' is read in the modern geological sense: islands that arose from the sea floor and never had a continental land connection. That excludes continental fragments such as New Zealand, Madagascar, the Seychelles and Japan, which Darwin partly treated as oceanic. Fiji and New Caledonia are also excluded as ambiguous. 'Naturally absent' is read as no native species. 'Introduced frogs thrive' is read as AmphibiaWeb recording an established introduced population. This dataset can test the distributional pattern (absence of native amphibians) and the introduction premise. It cannot test the physiological mechanism (sea-water killing spawn), which would need separate salinity-tolerance experiments. This plan therefore tests only the empirical absence generalization and the thriving-when-introduced premise.

dataset.name: AmphibiaWeb
dataset.why_it_fits: AmphibiaWeb is a global amphibian species database. Each species account gives taxonomy, geographic distribution by country and region, and notes on introduced populations. Its search and download tools allow species lists to be exported by country or region. Fields used: species name, order (Anura/Caudata/Gymnophiona), country/region distribution, and native versus introduced status in the species account. These are compared against the pre-registered oceanic-island list to count native and introduced amphibian species per island.
